findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent AC4/step-4 wording ('ownership registries') with child 3199's stance that no ownership registry is read — either add an ownership-derived section to the generated docs or amend the parent AC to reference the secret-name/schema/deprecation inputs actually used.
evidence: Parent plan step 4: 'Generate the config precedence/source/lifecycle reference ... from schema plus ownership/secret-name registries'
Parent AC4: 'Generated config/security/operator docs are byte-current with schema/ownership registries'
Child 3199 Outcome: 'There is no discrete "ownership registry" (ownership is a DERIVED AST classification in scripts/check_config_ownership.py); the generator does NOT read it.'
findings.finding: Parent AC4 requires generated docs to be 'byte-current with schema/ownership registries' and the parent plan step 4 says docs are generated 'from schema plus ownership/secret-name registries', but child 3199 explicitly states there is NO discrete ownership registry and its generator does NOT read one (inputs are only _config_schema, _deprecations.REGISTRY+tombstones, and _child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES). The observable topic coverage is delivered, but the 'ownership registries' derivation clause of AC4 is not covered as worded — a conflicting assumption between the parent's premise (an ownership registry exists to generate from) and the child's (ownership is a derived AST classification only).
scenarios: Completion verifier checks AC4's 'byte-current with ... ownership registries' clause and finds no ownership-registry input in the generator
A reviewer expects the generated security doc to enumerate approved owners/seams derived from the ownership gate's registry, but it is absent
findings.suggested_fix: Amend parent AC4/step-4 to say docs derive from schema + deprecation/secret-name registries (dropping 'ownership registries'), OR have child 3199 also render the approved-owner/seam table from check_config_ownership.py's registry so the 'ownership registries' clause is genuinely covered.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the ownership gate's scan boundary explicitly and reconcile it with the 'real tree' AC and the test-only-entry rule (e.g. name the scanned root(s), and say whether test/script trees are in scope or out of scope for both the below-seam prohibition and the exact path+symbol+rationale requirement).
evidence: Plan step 1: 'Reject direct/aliased load_config, os.getenv, ... below those seams' with no stated scan boundary
AC: 'The real tree has no direct ambient config/credential read, backend reload, or configurable adapter default below approved seams'

The existing gate scans a single root (check_config_ownership.py main defaults --root to src/rebar and rglob's *.py under it); test/scripts trees outside that root are never visited, so a below-seam read there is neither flagged nor required to carry an exception entry
Plan step 2 requires test-only controls to have 'exact path+symbol+rationale entries' — only meaningful for files the scanner actually visits
findings.finding: The ownership gate's coverage scope (the scanned source root) is not stated, but the acceptance criteria assert properties over 'the real tree' and require test-only controls to carry exact path+symbol+rationale entries; code outside the scan root is invisible to the gate rather than requiring an entry, so those claims hold only within an unstated boundary.
findings.location: Plan step 1-2 and AC 'The real tree has no direct ambient config/credential read... below approved seams' / 'Test-only controls and protocol constants require exact path+symbol+rationale entries'
scenarios: A future ambient os.getenv/credential read added under tests/ or scripts/ (which can import product paths) passes the gate silently, contradicting the 'real tree' AC
A reviewer reads the AC as a whole-repo guarantee and does not realize test-only entries are only required within the scanned root
